objective: Implement a CareOps staged-allocation lifecycle that consumes single-resource grant/release outcomes, makes partial claims and rollback explicit, and never claims atomic multi-resource allocation.
steps: Add behavior-first tests for deterministic staged claim requests, contending operations, deadline-at-grant timeout precedence, rejection, cancellation, expiry, rollback release failures, late grants, stale completion, segment-boundary interruption, FIFO issuance and non-interruptible work.
Implement a bounded pure CareOps state machine around single-resource grant/release results; keep acquired leases visible until release acknowledgement and retain failed-release residuals.
Treat deadline <= grant time as timeout; late/stale grants become explicit orphan releases. Idempotent cancel/expire and stale completion must not mutate current work.
Implement in-process suspend/resume only at explicit segment boundary; do not claim portable checkpoint/restart or Kairos atomic bundles.

Add a dev-only pinned-Kairos conformance test: use a capacity-one Flow resource with two contending CareOps claim tokens, bind exact engine request/resource identities, prove only one active lease exists, then release and prove the queued request grants.
Run focused CareOps allocator and Kairos conformance tests, core clippy and formatting; record exact outputs and source hashes. Defer full workspace compatibility to A3.4.

verification.oracle: Staged lifecycle cases pass and a pinned-Kairos Flow contention fixture proves a capacity-one resource never has two active leases.
CareOps core targets pass clippy with warnings denied.

acceptance: Every acquired lease remains visible until its release is acknowledged; failed rollback remains explicit and retryable.
Deadline-at-grant ties timeout; late grants are tracked and released rather than lost.
Cancellation, expiry, rejection and duplicate release/completion handling are idempotent or fail without state mutation.
Each accepted lease receipt matches the bound engine request identity, request revision and mapped resource identity.
A pinned-Kairos capacity-one contention fixture proves exclusive active leases and queued grant after release.

Request issuance order is deterministic FIFO among operations ready to issue their next claim; later arrivals cannot overtake an earlier ready waiter. This bounds only CareOps issuance and makes no guarantee about engine grants or capacity availability.

Urgency/priority is not an interruption input. Non-interruptible work rejects suspension without mutation; interruption occurs only between declared work segments and retains claims/progress through in-process suspend/resume.

No atomic multi-resource grant, portable checkpoint, ED schema/default, production dependency/runtime graph change, dependency upgrade, Kairos source or pin change is claimed; the test-only dependency on the exact pinned local Kairos crate is permitted.
stop_conditions: Pinned Kairos API differs from ADR-0011
True atomic multi-resource grant is required
Could not retain residual claims after failed release
size_exception: Reviewed bounded cross-file integration: A3.2 couples one CareOps coordinator module with a dev-only dependency and a pinned-Kairos conformance fixture. The exact write paths cover that module, its contract/conformance tests, and the minimum Cargo manifests/lock needed to verify real single-resource contention; no Kairos source or ED consumer files are included.
